payout_quote: It's completely free to list your space. ... We charge Hosts a small fee of 5% (incl. VAT) that's deducted from your gross earnings for each booking. Your gross earnings are calculated by deducting the Renter Fee from the total price paid by the Renter.
steps: Sign up on Stashbee and create a free host listing for your spare room, garage, loft, warehouse, or parking space with photos and your own price.
Pass Stashbee's ID verification; discuss access rules and approved items with potential renters via platform messaging.
Accept a booking; Stashbee collects the monthly payment from the renter and processes payment, invoicing, and contracts.
Receive your payout of gross earnings (total renter payment minus the 20% renter fee) with the 5% host fee deducted.
catches: The real cut is deeper than 5%: Stashbee first adds a 20% renter fee (25% for hourly bookings) to your set price, so your 'gross earnings' are calculated after that fee; then a 5% (incl. VAT) host fee is deducted - you keep roughly 95% of the post-renter-fee amount, i.e. about 79% of what the renter actually pays.
Earnings are demand- and location-driven: city storage/parking space near transport hubs earns; suburban attics may sit empty.
You are trusting strangers with access to your property - Stashbee offers ID verification and an Item Guarantee, but read its limits; homeowners' insurance often excludes commercial activity.
Renters may need access visits; agree rules upfront (access hours, banned items).
Stashbee is UK-focused; US coverage is thinner.
Storage income is taxable; hosts must ensure they have the right to sublet (renters/leasehold, planning permission for commercial storage).
Older Stashbee crowdfunding copy claimed a '20% service fee on each monthly transaction' - the current official help centre's 5% host fee / 20% renter fee split supersedes it.
biggest_catch: Stashbee keeps 5% of your earnings AND charges renters a 20-25% fee on top of your price, so the total platform take is far larger than the headline host fee - and your actual income depends entirely on local demand for your specific space.
eligibility: Own or control suitable space (spare room, garage, loft, warehouse, parking); pass ID verification; must have the right to rent it out (owner or landlord permission). UK-focused service.
timing: Listing free and self-serve; monthly bookings with payments collected by Stashbee and paid out to hosts. First booking depends on location demand and can take weeks or months.
weasel_words: hosts who store 20 boxes can earn 960 GBP per year
